With debug on, the plugin wrote packet-level TRACE dumps to plugins/AuditTrail/debug/trace-N.log at ~40-50 MB per ~10 s, rolling to a new file each time; the 443 MB volume went from 23 MB (5%) to 159 MB (36%) in about a minute and would have filled the disk.
args.actions: 1) Baseline status/logs/fs_du; noticed disk jump 23MB->66MB in 30s. 2) fs_du located plugins/AuditTrail/debug/trace-0.log (51MB) and server log showed 'AuditTrail config reloaded (debug=true)' at 06:51:21. 3) Declared incident. 4) Read config.yml (debug: true), listed debug dir, sampled trace content (TRACE packet spam, no user data), checked 'help audittrail'. 5) Wrote config.yml back to 'debug: false / retention-days: 30'. 6) Ran console 'audittrail' (returned usage but also reloaded, logged at 06:51:55) then 'audittrail reload' (logged 06:52:01); both confirmed debug=false. 7) Verified trace files stopped growing (mtimes frozen at 06:51:55, identical sizes after 15s wait) and config unchanged. 8) Deleted trace-0.log, trace-1.log, trace-2.log (~132 MB total). 9) Verified disk back to 23 MB (5%), debug dir empty, TPS 20.0, all plugins enabled, both players still online, over two further wait windows (~60s).
args.residual_risk: Whoever/whatever flipped debug: true was not identified (no player command in the log; it was a file edit plus a reload, likely an operator or an automated process). If it is re-enabled, the fill will recur within minutes at ~5 MB/s. Recommend the team find the source of the 06:51:19 config edit, add a disk-usage alert, and consider having AuditTrail cap/rotate its debug output. Heap rose 352->467 MB of 768 MB over the shift, which looks like normal GC behaviour but is worth a glance on the next shift.
